# Catalog rules and their implementation

The catalog in [TRANSLATION_RULES.md](TRANSLATION_RULES.md) numbers **38 rules** in seven
families. The engine implements them as **25 matcher entries** in
[`src/engine/rules.ts`](../src/engine/rules.ts). The two numberings differ on purpose:

* **One matcher can realise several catalog rules.** `UNION-pair` matches
  `R ≔ R ∪ {a ↦ b}` and then dispatches on the container chosen for `R`, so it is
  `PS2` for a pair-set, `FN3` for a function and `MS2` for a map-of-sets. `CLEAR`
  covers every family's "reset to empty" rule at once.
* **One catalog rule can need several matchers.** `FN3` appears as both `FN3-app`
  (`f(k) ≔ v`) and `FN3-override` (`f ≔ f  {k ↦ v}`), because Event-B spells the
  same update two ways.
* **Two families are not in this file at all.** `ENC1`–`ENC6` choose the container and
  live in [`src/engine/encodingResolver.ts`](../src/engine/encodingResolver.ts);
  `ST1`–`ST5` are structural (event → guarded `bool` method, typing guards dropped)
  and are applied by [`src/engine/codeEmitter.ts`](../src/engine/codeEmitter.ts) and
  `translateEvent` in [`src/engine/ruleEngine.ts`](../src/engine/ruleEngine.ts).

Catalog rules named by the matchers below: `CMP1`, `CMP2`, `FN1`, `FN2`, `FN3`, `FN4`, `FN5`, `MS1`, `MS2`, `MS3`, `MS4`, `MS5`, `MS6`, `MS7`, `MS8`, `PS1`, `PS2`, `PS3`, `PS4`, `PS5`, `PS6`, `PS7`, `SET1`, `SET2`, `SET3`, `SET4`, `SET5`.

| Implementation id | Catalog rule(s) | Shape it matches |
|---|---|---|
| `CMP2` | `CMP2` | f ≔ (A ∖ B) × {const} (incl. const = ∅) |
| `CLEAR` | `FN5`, `SET5`, `PS7`, `MS8` | X ≔ ∅ (FN5/SET5/PS7/MS8) |
| `MS7` | `MS7` | M ≔ M ∪ ({k} × s) |
| `MS2` | `MS2` | f(k) ≔ f(k) ∪ {x} |
| `MS3-fn` | `MS3` | f(k) ≔ f(k) ∖ {x} |
| `FN3-app` | `FN3` | f(k) ≔ v |
| `FN3-override` | `FN3` | f ≔ f {k↦v}. THREE SPELLINGS OCCUR IN REAL PROJECTS and all must be accepted: U+E103 Rodin's private-use codepoint. It renders as nothing outside Rodin, so it also survives as a bare space in copied text. U+2295 ⊕ what a plain Rodin export of this project's own pM1 contains. Found 2026-08-10 by generating from the pristine export and getting one more UNTRANSLATED than from the working copy. U+22B4 ⊴ a legacy spelling. Missing a spelling does not fail loudly: the action goes untranslated and the event refuses to fire, which reads as a gap in the MODEL, not in the parser. |
| `UNION-pair` | `PS2`, `FN3`, `MS2` | pair-set insert (PS2), function-extend (FN3), or map-of-sets per-key insert (MS2's pair spelling) — dispatched by enc |
| `DIFF-pair` | `PS3`, `MS3`, `FN4` | pair-set erase (PS3), map-of-sets per-key remove (MS3), or function-shrink (FN4, the mirror of the union case above) — dispatched by enc. A function is a map keyed by `a`, so removing the maplet means erasing key `a` — but only when it currently maps to `b`, since Event-B set-minus removes nothing if the pair is absent. Without this case a function fell through to `R.erase({a, b})`, which does not compile against std::map. |

Guards and actions are matched by the same array: `translateEvent` tries every rule
once per clause, in the order above, and takes the first that matches. There is no
recursion into subexpressions — see the *catalog matches shapes, and does not nest*
limitation in the paper.
